skill.name: code-review-and-quality
skill.description: Provides a structured code review workflow across correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance, tests, and change readiness.
skill.summary: Review code changes with clear quality gates before merge.
skill.author: addyosmani

content.value_statement: Code changes often miss risks when review criteria are informal. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured review process with actionable findings.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates code changes across correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance.
Checks whether tests cover behavior, edge cases, and regression risks.
Labels review findings by severity so authors know what blocks merge.
Identifies oversized changes and suggests practical split strategies.
Reviews dependency additions for necessity, maintenance, vulnerability, and license concerns.
Provides a reusable review checklist for pull requests and agent-generated code.
limitations: It is a review workflow, not an automated static analyzer.
It depends on access to the code, tests, requirements, and verification evidence.
It can miss issues that require domain knowledge or production telemetry.
Referenced security and performance checklist files are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Review pull requests before merge
use_cases.description: Apply consistent criteria before approving or requesting changes on a code review.

use_cases.title: Audit AI-generated code
use_cases.description: Check model-written changes for correctness, maintainability, security, and missing tests.

use_cases.title: Improve team review standards
use_cases.description: Create a shared checklist and severity language for reliable review feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Change Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing a small pull request or local diff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code change for correctness, readability, tests, and obvious security issues. List blocking issues first, then optional suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Against a Requirement
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the change should implement a specific task or specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change against the stated requirement. Check whether the behavior matches the requirement, edge cases are handled, and tests prove the behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture and Maintainability Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a change touches shared modules, abstractions, or large files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for architecture, module boundaries, duplication, file size, and unnecessary complexity. Propose simpler structural remedies for each major concern.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging a high-impact or security-sensitive change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release readiness review across correctness, security, performance, dependency risk, tests, and verification evidence. Separate critical, required, optional, and nit findings.

output_examples.input: Review a bug fix that changes validation logic and adds tests.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review with required correctness issues first, then test coverage notes and optional readability suggestions.

output_examples.input: Review a large refactor that moves code across modules.
output_examples.output: A structural review that checks whether complexity was reduced, boundaries stayed clear, and the change should be split.

output_examples.input: Review a dependency addition before merge.
output_examples.output: A dependency assessment covering necessity, existing alternatives, maintenance status, vulnerability checks, and license compatibility.

best_practices: Provide the diff, related tests, requirements, and verification notes before asking for review.
Ask the reviewer to separate blocking findings from optional suggestions.
Use the checklist before approval, especially for security-sensitive or large changes.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to approve code without reading the implementation and tests.
Treating style preferences as blocking issues without a team standard.
Reviewing a large unrelated changeset as one unit instead of asking for a split.

faq.question: Can this skill replace human code review?
faq.answer: No. It improves review consistency, but a responsible human should make final merge decisions.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks for test and build evidence, but tool execution depends on the host agent and project context.

faq.question: What kinds of issues does it prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes correctness, security, structural regressions, and missed simplifications before cosmetic feedback.

faq.question: Is it useful for AI-generated code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow explicitly covers code written by agents, models, humans, or the reviewer.

faq.question: Does it include security-specific guidance?
faq.answer: It includes security review prompts and checks, but detailed referenced checklist files are not included.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before merging pull requests, after bug fixes, after refactors, and before release-critical changes.
